findings.how: Unchanged since round 1, and the verifier raised nothing here. Reproduced on Xvfb: with setxkbmap ctrl:nocaps, Caps+Alt+Space read {control:false}, so freshAskPress returned false. x11.keysDown() now takes Ctrl and Alt from two sources: the modifier state the server reports (XQueryPointer's ControlMask/Mod1Mask, the same state Electron's grab matched on), or any held keycode whose level-0 keysym is Control_L/R or Alt_L/R (XKeycodeToKeysym). It no longer uses XKeysymToKeycode, which returns only the lowest keycode for a keysym. The logic is a pure export, chordHeld(mask, held, symOf). After the fix the Xvfb script gives the right answer for ctrl:nocaps, ctrl:swapcaps, altwin:swap_alt_win and altwin:alt_win, and nothing held is still rejected. With Electron 44's real globalShortcut under ctrl:nocaps, the Caps chord opens the ask box.

findings.how:
Round 1 (a7af91d): reproduced on Xvfb with AccessX set the way GNOME sets it. Slow Keys typed nothing but the borrow reported done, Bounce Keys gave 'helo world', and Ember's Ctrl+A switched Sticky Keys (TwoKeys) off. The optional XInput.keyboardBlockedReason(keys?) reads XkbControlsRec.enabled_ctrls. If Slow, Bounce or Sticky Keys is on it returns TYPING_ASSIST_REASON; with no XKB it returns null. The borrow asks it before the first key of keys() and type(), and in checkTyping(). Clicks and scrolls don't ask, and the user's setting is never changed. The check-up shows a 'Typing' warn row while it refuses.

Round 2 (767ac7c), the verifier was right: on the default paste path the refusal came only after Ember had acted. Replace and append glided and clicked first. Insert wrote Ember's text to the clipboard, then waited pasteWaitMs. Fix: a new Hand.checkKeys(combo). It reads the combination with the same helper keys() uses (comboKeys) and calls keyboardUsable({modifiers, sym}), pressing nothing, so macOS still lets Command+V through under an input method. In worker.ts's cursor_text path, the callback now checks every combo it will press (select-all and Delete for replace, text-end for append, paste when pasting) next to checkTyping. That is before the first glide or click, and before clipboard.writeText. Now all three modes refuse with nothing clicked, pressed or written, and with no paste wait.

One gap from the verifier's description is left, outside its fix: a keys-only borrow (press_keys) still brings the target window to the front before keys() refuses. No key is sent, and when the borrow ends restoreFocus() gives the keyboard back to the window the user was in. Refusing before the raise would need the combination in the borrow's preflight, for example a BorrowOptions.keys checked next to blockedReason, which changes withCursor's signature in worker.ts. I propose that for a later round.

Correction to my round-1 report: 'the worker's up-front text check refuses before any click' was true only on the non-paste path and in fillCell. Now it is true on the paste path too.

findings.how:
Round 1 (580f3e0) added CursorBorrow.stopForQuit(). It stops the borrow, and the borrow driving at that moment releases every key and button, moves the pointer home and gives the keyboard back, all synchronously. Main's input will-quit called it before xinput.close().

The verifier was right that only the pointer half worked in the real app. main.ts registers the window system's will-quit (ws.close) before the input's, so the window system was already closed when stopForQuit() ran. Main's mayRefocus asks shownWindows() over wsRef.stack(), and a closed X11, Win32 or darwin window system returns []. So the keyboard stayed on the target. My round-1 unit test and q1 script passed no mayRefocus, which hid this.

Round 2 (bbec53a): main.ts's window-system will-quit is now `app.on("will-quit", () => { borrowRef?.stopForQuit(); ws?.close(); });`. The hand-back runs while the window system can still list the window. The input's handler later calls stopForQuit() again; handBack is null by then, so it only stops, then the input closes. The stopForQuit() doc comment now says where main calls it.

On Xvfb with mutter, a real openX11 window system and main's mayRefocus (my copy of the verifier's q2.ts, plus a main-fixed order):
- main's old order: pointer home, focus still on the target (FAIL).
- main's new order (stopForQuit, ws.close, stopForQuit, x.close): pointer home {2073,1296} and focus back where the user was, PASS twice.
- borrow-first order: PASS (its first run failed during startup timing, with the pointer never reaching the glide target; the re-run passed).

The endSession path (power-monitor shutdown, Windows session-end) is unchanged on purpose: it still calls borrowRef.stop() and inputRef.releaseAll(), so keys and buttons come up but the pointer and the keyboard are not given back. The session is ending anyway.

Correction: 580f3e0's subject and my round-1 report said the keyboard went back. It did only while the window system was still open. Since bbec53a it does when Ember quits through will-quit.

verifierProblems.what: Only the pointer half of #66 is fixed in the real app. The keyboard still stays on the target after a quit mid-borrow. main.ts registers `app.on("will-quit", () => ws?.close())` at line 1210, before the borrow's handler at line 1366 (both in whenReady, so they run in that order). So the window system is already closed when stopForQuit() runs. handBack's restoreFocus() asks main's mayRefocus, which is `shownWindows().some(...)` over `wsRef?.stack()`. A closed X11, Win32 or darwin window system returns [] from stack() (`if (!open) return [];`), so mayRefocus says false and the previous window is never activated. The new unit test (borrow-quit.test.ts) and the fix agent's q1 script both pass no mayRefocus, which hid this. My scratch script relfix-verify/input/scripts/q2.ts uses Xvfb, mutter, a real openX11 window system and main's mayRefocus. In main's order (ws.close, stopForQuit, x.close) the fix gives pointer home {2073,1296} but focus still on the target: FAIL. With stopForQuit before ws.close it gives pointer home and focus back where the user was: PASS. The base fails both ways. Commit 580f3e0 and the report say 'the keyboard back'.
verifierProblems.fix: Hand back before the window system closes. For example, change main.ts:1210 to `app.on("will-quit", () => { borrowRef?.stopForQuit(); ws?.close(); });`. stopForQuit() is idempotent: the later call at line 1366 finds handBack null and only stops, then xinput.close() runs. Alternatively, register the borrow and input handler with app.prependListener("will-quit", ...). List the hunk as shared. Add a unit test whose mayRefocus reads a window list that empties when the window system closes, driven in main's real order, so the ordering stays pinned. Correct the commit and report wording once it passes.

verifierProblems.what: On the default typing path, the keyboard refusal comes only after Ember has already acted. Local cursor_text uses paste whenever a clipboard is available (worker.ts:2041), and checkTyping is skipped for paste (worker.ts:2104). Under Typing Assist, mode replace or append glides and clicks into the field, and only then does keys(selectAll) or keys(textEnd) refuse. Mode insert first writes Ember's text to the user's clipboard and sets pasting.pressed = true. Then keys(paste) refuses, and the finally waits pasteWaitMs for a paste that never comes before restoring the clipboard. keysOnly borrows (press_keys) also bring the target window to the front before the first key refuses. The report says 'the worker's up-front text check refuses before any click', which is true only on the non-paste path and in fillCell. The scenario itself is gone: nothing is lost or changed and Sticky Keys stays on.
verifierProblems.fix: Give the Hand a no-key check, for example `checkKeys(combo)`: parse it and call keyboardUsable({modifiers, sym}) without pressing anything, so macOS still lets Cmd+V through under an input method. In worker.ts's cursor_text path, call it for the select-all, text-end and paste combos it will press, before the first glide or click and before clipboard.writeText. That is a small shared hunk in worker.ts. A unit test should check that no click and no clipboard write happen while keyboardBlockedReason refuses.
